title: Comprehensive Omics Analysis of a Novel Small-Molecule Inhibitor of Chemoresistant Oncogenic Signatures in Colorectal Cancer Cell with Antitumor Effects.
authors: Huang, Tse-Hung; Mokgautsi, Ntlotlang; Huang, Yan-Jiun; Wu, Alexander T H; Huang, Hsu-Shan
one_liner_zh: 该文通过组学与分子对接分析小分子抑制剂RV59靶向结直肠癌中MYC/CXCL8/TIMP1致癌通路，虽涉及MYC转录因子与DNA互作背景，但核心是药物抗肿瘤效应，缺乏TF-DNA结合建模与AI/物理模拟方法。
abstract: Tumor recurrence from cancer stem cells (CSCs) and metastasis often occur post-treatment in colorectal cancer (CRC), leading to chemoresistance and resistance to targeted therapy. MYC is a transcription factor in the nuclei that modulates cell growth and development, and regulates immune response in an antitumor direction by mediating programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1) and promoting CRC tumor recurrence after adjuvant chemotherapy. However, the molecular mechanism through which c-MYC maintains stemness and confers treatment resistance still remains elusive in CRC. In addition, recent reports demonstrated that CRC solid colon tumors expresses C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 8 (CXCL8). Expression of CXCL8 in CRC was reported to activate the expression of PD-L1 immune checkpoint through c-MYC, this ultimately induces chemoresistance in CRC. Accumulating studies have also demonstrated increased expression of CXCL8, matrix metalloproteinase 7 (MMP7), tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase 1 (TIMP1), and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) components, in CRC tumors suggesting their potential collaboration to promote EMT and CSCs. TIMP1 is MMP-independent and regulates cell development and apoptosis in various cancer cell types, including CRC. Recent studies showed that TIMP1 cleaves CXCL8 on its chemoattractant, thereby influencing its mechanistic response to therapy. This therefore suggests crosstalk among the c-MYC/CXCL8/TIMP1 oncogenic signatures. In this study, we explored computer simulations through bioinformatics to identify and validate that the MYC/CXCL8/TIMP1 oncogenic signatures are overexpressed in CRC, Moreover, our docking results exhibited putative binding affinities of the above-mentioned oncogenes, with our novel small molecule, RV59, Finally, we demonstrated the anticancer activities of RV59 against NCI human CRC cancer cell lines both as single-dose and dose-dependent treatments, and also demonstrated the MYC/CXCL8/TIMP1 signaling pathway as a potential RV59 drug target.
abstract_zh: 肿瘤干细胞（CSCs）导致的肿瘤复发和转移常发生在结直肠癌（CRC）治疗之后，导致化疗耐药和靶向治疗耐药。MYC是细胞核中的一种转录因子，调节细胞生长和发育，并通过介导程序性死亡配体1（PD-L1）以抗肿瘤方向调节免疫反应，同时促进CRC在辅助化疗后的肿瘤复发。然而，c-MYC在CRC中维持干性和赋予治疗耐药的分子机制仍不清楚。此外，近期报告表明，CRC实体结肠肿瘤表达C-X-C基序趋化因子配体8（CXCL8）。据报道，CRC中CXCL8的表达通过c-MYC激活PD-L1免疫检查点的表达，这最终诱导CRC的化疗耐药。越来越多的研究也表明，CRC肿瘤中CXCL8、基质金属蛋白酶7（MMP7）、金属蛋白酶组织抑制剂1（TIMP1）和上皮-间质转化（EMT）成分的表达增加，提示它们可能协同促进EMT和CSCs。TIMP1不依赖MMP，并在包括CRC在内的多种癌细胞类型中调节细胞发育和凋亡。近期研究表明，TIMP1在其趋化因子位点切割CXCL8，从而影响其对治疗的反应机制。因此，这提示c-MYC/CXCL8/TIMP1致癌特征之间存在串扰。在本研究中，我们通过生物信息学探索计算机模拟，以识别并验证MYC/CXCL8/TIMP1致癌特征在CRC中过表达。此外，我们的对接结果显示上述致癌基因与我们的新型小分子RV59具有推定结合亲和力。最后，我们证明了RV59对NCI人CRC癌细胞系的抗癌活性，包括单剂量和剂量依赖性处理，并证明了MYC/CXCL8/TIMP1信号通路是RV59的潜在药物靶点。
